newsitem.title: USA: PP&L sees Pa. 1,090 MW nuke back fully Wed.
newsitem.headline: PP&L sees Pa. 1,090 MW nuke back fully Wed.

text.p: Pennsylvania Power & Light Co (PP&L) said Monday it expected the 1,090 megawatt (MW) unit 1 at the Susquehanna generating station to reach full power Wednesday.
PP&L idled the Berwick, Pa., unit on October 28 to repair a small leak in a steam drain pipe inside the reactor building following a 47-day refueling and maintenance outage.
"The work has been completed. We're on test schedule after the refueling," a PP&L spokesman said.
The neighboring 1,094 MW Susquehanna unit 2 was generating at 100 percent output, he said, adding the slight overflow along the Susquehanna River this weekend did not affect the station's operation.
The two Susquehanna units are jointly owned by PP&L and Allegheny Electric Cooperative Inc.
The Susquehanna complex accounts for 30 percent of PP&L power deliveries and 20 percent of its installed generation capacity.
